label: 4th original token (t=3), gated by a favored 3-token prefix (z/e/t/g, then 0, then d/w/o/m)
explanation: Fires only at step t=3 (the 4th original input, so L>=4). It never fires on any other step, the delimiter or the copy phase. Within t=3 it fires on about 17% of sequences. Whether it fires, and how strongly, depends roughly additively on the three preceding tokens: first token e/t/g/z (about 2-3x lift), second token 0 (4.3x), third token d/w/o/m (2-4x). The top activations (about 0.5-0.56) are all on the prefix z 0 o, where all three cues are present. The current token matters little, and the feature is weaker when the current token repeats an earlier one. The OR of the three cues gets dev F1 about 0.50 and mass recall 0.75. Requiring 2 of 3 cues raises precision to about 0.51 at lower recall. So this is a t=3 position feature with a distributed prefix preference that a simple boolean predicate only partly captures.

scorecard.summary: Weighted combination of 40 cues. Raise it: orig_idx=3 (+6.20), t=3 (+4.17), t=3 & prev_tok=d (+3.83), t=3 & prev_tok=w (+2.65), prev3_tok=t (+2.44), prev3_tok=g (+1.96). Lower it: orig_idx=-1 (-4.13), orig1=t (-3.64), orig0=c (-2.76), in_first=0 (-2.38).
